subject: Culture
title: Pride's Riot Origins
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Pride's Riot Origins.

hook.text: Pride Month started with a riot. On June 28, 1969, police raided the Stonewall Inn. Patrons fought back.

buildup.text: Before Stonewall, being openly gay in the US could mean arrest, job loss, and psychiatric commitment.

discovery.text: Marsha P. Johnson and Sylvia Rivera, both trans women of color, became icons of the uprising.

twist.text: Modern Pride parades feature corporate floats. Some activists say commercialization erased the protest roots.

climax.text: Pride began as a fight for survival. Whether it stays that or becomes a parade depends on memory.

punchline.text: The first Pride was a brick, not a float.

quiz.question: What 1969 event sparked the modern Pride movement?

details.summary: Pride celebrations trace directly to the 1969 Stonewall Riots, when LGBTQ+ patrons of a New York bar fought back against a police raid. What began as an uprising against police harassment became a global movement. Pride parades memorialize resistance, not just celebration.
details.whyItMatters: Pride's riot origins remind us that LGBTQ+ rights were won through resistance, not granted through tolerance. Understanding this history reframes Pride from party to political anniversary.
takeaways: The Stonewall Riots erupted on June 28, 1969, in New York City
Trans women of color, including Marsha P. Johnson, led early resistance
The first Pride marches in 1970 were protest marches, not parades

faq.question: What happened at Stonewall?
faq.answer: On June 28, 1969, police raided the Stonewall Inn, a gay bar in Greenwich Village. Instead of complying as usual, patrons fought back. Six days of protests followed. Key figures included Marsha P. Johnson and Sylvia Rivera, both transgender women of color.

faq.question: How did Pride evolve from protest to celebration?
faq.answer: The first Pride marches in 1970 were explicitly political protests demanding rights and visibility. Over decades, as legal protections expanded, Pride incorporated celebration alongside activism. Critics debate whether corporate sponsorship has diluted Pride's radical origins.
